title: Minesweeper
summary: Given an m x n board with unrevealed mines ('M'), empty squares ('E'), revealed blanks ('B'), and revealed mines ('X'), and a click position, reveal the board according to these rules: If 'M' is revealed, change it to 'X' and end the game.
statement: Given an m x n board with unrevealed mines ('M'), empty squares ('E'), revealed blanks ('B'), and revealed mines ('X'), and a click position, reveal the board according to these rules: If 'M' is revealed, change it to 'X' and end the game. If 'E' with no adjacent mines is revealed, change it to 'B' and reveal all adjacent 'E'. If 'E' has at least one adjacent mine, change it to the count of adjacent mines ('1' to '8'). Return the board when no more squares can be revealed.
constraints: 1 <= rows, columns <= 50. Input cells are M (unrevealed mine), E (unrevealed empty), B (revealed blank), or a digit 1..8.
click=[row,column] is in bounds and points to M or E. Input boards contain no X; clicking M creates X and changes no other cell.
Mine counts and expansion use all EIGHT neighbors, including diagonals. A revealed numbered cell stops expansion; a blank B expands to adjacent unrevealed empty cells.
Return the resulting rectangular board. Existing revealed cells and unclicked mines remain unchanged. Returning a correctly updated copy is also allowed.
hints: Revealing a blank recursively exposes neighbors, but a number forms a stopping boundary.
Use DFS or BFS from the click. Count adjacent mines before deciding whether to expand.
If clicked M set X and stop. Otherwise pop an E cell, count eight neighbors; write a digit if nonzero, else B and enqueue unseen E neighbors.
Mark queued cells to prevent repeated work. An explicit stack has the same recursive flood-fill behavior without overflowing Python on a 50-by-50 empty board.
editorial: Only zero-adjacent-mine empty cells propagate the reveal. Their connected component and its adjacent empty boundary determine every changed cell. The explicit stack implements the recursive rule, while a queued set ensures each cell is processed once. Every cell has at most eight neighbors, giving O(rows*columns) time and space. The independent oracle constructs connected components with union-find and reveals the selected component plus its numbered boundary rather than simulating the stack.

tests.explanation: The bottom-left empty region expands through blanks and stops at numbered cells beside the mine. E at [0,2] stays hidden behind that numbered boundary; expansion does not cross a numbered cell.
The clicked M becomes X. Every other cell, including the still-hidden E above it and all already-revealed cells, remains unchanged.
